tuition_notes: Public art university - no tuition stated; a 50.00 EUR application fee applies (plus international transfer costs). Semester fee amount TBC.
application_deadline: Winter semester: 15 April; Summer semester: 15 November
deadline_source_cycle: TBC - dates given without a year
entry_requirements_summary: Bachelor's degree or diploma in Sound Engineering (Tonmeister) from UdK Berlin or an equivalent programme elsewhere, plus demonstrated artistic talent. Portfolio of at least five audio/video productions uploaded to Bemus, including at least one classical and one popular-music production. Entrance examination with a mixing task and an oral examination.
red_flags: ELIGIBILITY BLOCKER: admission requires a bachelor/diploma specifically in Sound Engineering (Tonmeister) or an equivalent programme - a software-engineering diploma does not qualify. German C1. Portfolio of five professional productions plus a live mixing entrance exam. Logged for completeness, not as a realistic target.
fit_notes: Berlin's flagship recording-arts master, taught jointly with TU Berlin's audio engineering courses, tuition-free. Excellent subject fit in principle but effectively closed to anyone without a Tonmeister bachelor. Only 2 semesters/60 ECTS.

program_name: Creative Production (Music), MA
degree_awarded: MA validated by Plymouth Marjon University (UK)
institution: Catalyst - Institute for Creative Arts and Technology, Berlin
english_level_required: IELTS 6.0 equivalent / B2, or Catalyst's own 90-minute online test
tuition_notes: Full-time international: 6,028 EUR per semester over 2 semesters, or 11,693 EUR paid annually (3% discount). Part-time: 3,678 EUR/semester over 4 semesters, or 7,134 EUR annually. Non-refundable enrolment fee 895 EUR per study year.
application_deadline: 30 April 2026 (visa-required applicants); 5 June 2026 (EU/visa-exempt); 28 August 2026 late, subject to availability; course starts mid-September 2026
entry_requirements_summary: Bachelor's degree in a relevant discipline at honours level (UK 2:1 equivalent); non-standard entry considered on professional or life experience. Portfolio and project proposal required.
scholarship_names: 1,000 EUR tuition discount for priority-deadline applicants; 500 EUR discount for combining a summer course with the degree; BAföG and national schemes for eligible students
red_flags: The award is a UK degree validated by Plymouth Marjon University, NOT a German staatlich anerkannter Masterabschluss issued by Catalyst - this materially affects Tunisian student-visa issuance and later recognition in Germany/EU. Verify with the German embassy and with Catalyst in writing. 11,693 EUR/yr plus an 895 EUR enrolment fee, with only small percentage discounts as 'scholarships'. BAföG is not open to most non-EU students. Visa-required applicants must apply by 30 April - the earliest hard deadline in the Berlin set.
fit_notes: English-taught music production master inside the Funkhaus, in the heart of Berlin's electronic-music scene - culturally the best match for the DJ/producer half of the dual career, and the entry route is open (bachelor in any relevant discipline, or non-standard entry). Weakest on the FUNDING-FIRST criterion and on award status. Sits at the Path A / production-path boundary; the 'creative production' emphasis is more studio than DSP.

tuition_notes: German public universities - no tuition, Semesterbeitrag only. Amount not confirmed on an official page this session.
entry_requirements_summary: A professionally qualifying German or equivalent foreign university degree with at least 20 credit points earned in courses with musicological content, or equivalent. International applicants must evidence German proficiency.
red_flags: No FU/HU page was opened this session (search budget exhausted) - all content derives from search extracts. ELIGIBILITY BLOCKER: at least 20 credit points of musicological coursework required, which a software-engineering diploma does not provide. German-taught. Content is musicology/theatre/performance studies, not audio computing.
fit_notes: Included only to close the Humboldt/Berlin coverage question. It is not a sound-and-music-computing programme and the client is almost certainly ineligible. HU's Institut für Musikwissenschaft und Medienwissenschaft does host systematic musicology and media-technology research, so a follow-up should check the separate MA Medienwissenschaft for computational/audio content.
